q: How do I calculate the emissions of storing potatoes in cold storage per bag?
title: Potato cold storage emissions per bag
short: Take the cold store's electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25 and generator diesel at 2.68 kg per litre for the storage season, then divide by bag-months stored. A full store spreads the same refrigeration load over more bags, so occupancy changes the figure per bag.
audience: Cold storage owners, potato farmers and traders

p: Bags stay for different lengths of time. Multiply bags by months stored to share energy fairly between farmers or traders.
The store owner reports the electricity and diesel as Scope 2 and Scope 1. A farmer paying rent per bag reports it in Scope 3.

example.title: Worked example: one storage season (illustrative inputs)
lines: Total: 153,120 / 120,000 = 1.276 kg CO2 per bag a month
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use the store's bills and stock register.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
